items.title: Carney Has Canadians’ Support on Trump. Now Comes the Hard Part.
items.author: Matina Stevis-Gridneff
items.content: <article>The U.S.-Canada trade war has galvanized Canadians behind their prime minister’s decision to walk away from negotiations. What happens when the time comes for talks to restart?</article>

items.title: Trump Says U.S. Struck Deal for Control of More Than 65 Billion Barrels of Venezuela’s Oil
items.author: Rebecca F. Elliott, Simon Romero and Edward Wong
items.content: <article>The president said an agreement between the countries covered more than 65 billion barrels of reserves. A U.S. official said it would involve a partnership with a private company.</article>

items.title: Sweden’s Far-Right Leader Seeks a Comeback as Election Nears
items.author: Charlie Duxbury
items.content: <article>Swedish far-right leader Jimmie Akesson kicked off the final two weeks of a tight election campaign with a speech in his home town aimed rallying supporters and closing a consistent polling gap.</article>

items.title: Teleprompter Operator Who Bet on Trump Speeches Is Ordered to Pay Fine
items.author: Luke Broadwater
items.content: <article>Gabriel Perez had access to the president’s speeches before they were delivered and was accused of placing unlawful wagers on words that would be spoken.</article>

items.title: High Debt and Rising Prices Catch Up to Trump, as Midterms Near
items.author: Tony Romm
items.content: <article>To win in 2024, the president promised an economic course correction. Almost two years later, his agenda has made that fight even harder.</article>

items.title: Niger Rulers Say Army Mutiny Contained After Gunfire in Capital
items.author: Kamailoudini Tagba and Ruth Olurounbi
items.content: <article>Niger said it contained a mutiny by soldiers who detained some of their colleagues at a military base and fired on sites in the capital, the first major challenge from within the armed forces to the junta that seized power three years ago.</article>

items.title: France’s Lecornu Warns Budget Impasse May Fuel Instability
items.author: Nayla Razzouk
items.content: <article>Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu warned that France needs to pass a budget ahead of presidential elections next year or risk plunging into political and financial instability.</article>

items.title: US Canada Trade Fight Shows Few Signs of Easing
items.content: <article>The US and Canada appear to be headed for a prolonged trade standoff, with no current negotiations and Canadian officials expecting serious talks may not resume until after the US midterm elections. Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Jeff Mason and Bloomberg News Executive Editor for Canada Derek Decloet are on Bloomberg This Weekend with Christina Ruffini and Bailey Lipschultz to discuss the economic pain on both sides of the border, Canada’s push to diversify its trade and whether Prime Minister Mark Carney’s resistance to President Donald Trump could influence how other US allies respond. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Judge Rules Trump Unlawfully Targeted Stanford Students Who Criticized Israel
items.author: Chris Cameron
items.content: <article>The ruling was a win for Stanford’s student newspaper, The Stanford Daily, and it followed another court victory for students targeted by the Trump administration last year.</article>

items.title: Trump Keeps Building His Ballroom Amid Supreme Court’s Silence
items.author: Greg Stohr
items.content: <article>Construction on President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom shows no signs of slowing down. And the US Supreme Court shows no signs of wanting to stop it.</article>

items.title: Trump Backlash Adds New Risks to the Stocks the Government Owns
items.author: Norah Rami and Matthew Griffin
items.content: <article>Traders have made a bundle over the past year following President Donald Trump as the US government pursues an unprecedented strategy of taking ownership stakes in publicly traded companies.</article>

items.title: Republicans See Trump’s Unceasing Iran War as Midterm Threat
items.author: Joshua Green and Nancy Cook
items.content: <article>Six months into a conflict that President Donald Trump predicted would last “four to five weeks,” Republican strategists worry there’s no way to keep the Iran war from hurting the party’s prospects in November’s midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Ukraine Says Russia Planning Ground Offensive on Kyiv, Chernihiv
items.author: Olesia Safronova
items.content: <article>Ukraine has received intelligence that Russia is preparing for a possible new ground offensive toward Kyiv as well as Chernihiv in the nation’s far north, a top official said.</article>

items.title: Death Toll at 37 From Russian Strike on Warehouse Near Kyiv
items.author: Olesia Safronova and Ros Krasny
items.content: <article>At least 37 people were killed in a village west of Kyiv when a warehouse detonated following a Russian drone strike, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy vowed an investigation into why explosives had been stored in a densely populated area.</article>

items.title: Fact-Checking Senate Races in Georgia, Alaska and Texas
items.author: Linda Qiu
items.content: <article>Candidates’ attacks are focused on illegal immigration, faith and stock trading.</article>

items.title: Iceland Votes in Tight Referendum on European Union Entry Talks
items.author: Ragnhildur Sigurdardottir and Ott Ummelas
items.content: <article>Icelanders voted on Saturday on whether to reopen membership talks with the European Union in a referendum that’s testing the bloc’s geopolitical appeal.</article>

items.title: Russia Is Teaching Its Children to Fight the Wars of the Future
items.author: Bloomberg News
items.content: <article>Students returning to Russian schools next week will discover a change to their civics courses that puts military training at the heart of the lessons.</article>

items.title: Reform UK Seeks to Play Down Crypto, Show Off Diplomatic Clout
items.author: Lucy White
items.content: <article>Reform UK is highlighting its diplomatic clout and de-emphasizing support from crypto companies as Nigel Farage’s populist party seeks to show that it’s ready to lead Britain.</article>

items.title: Hegseth Blocks Promotions of Four Army Officers as Purge Widens
items.author: Greg Jaffe, Eric Schmitt and Helene Cooper
items.content: <article>The turmoil has left a leadership vacuum in the Army at a moment when it is trying to find ways to defend troops against the threat posed by cheap drones.</article>

items.title: ICE Explores Purchasing Robot Dogs in Enforcement Tech Push
items.author: Alicia A. Caldwell
items.content: <article>The Trump administration is exploring adding robot dogs to the expanding arsenal being used by federal immigration authorities as they seek to boost arrests and deportations across the country.</article>

items.title: Trump Teleprompter Pays $170,000 to End Insider Trading Probe
items.author: Nicola M White
items.content: <article>A White House teleprompter operator will pay more than $172,000 to end a federal regulator’s probe into alleged well-timed prediction market bets about President Donald Trump’s speeches.</article>

items.title: Nepal Seeks Foreign Help as Scale of Flood Disaster Grows
items.author: Dan Strumpf, Kanupriya Kapoor and Akriti Sharma
items.content: <article>Nepal sought international help to cope with the aftermath of catastrophic flash floods that have left nearly 3,000 people missing along the mountainous border with China.</article>

items.title: US War With Iran Hits Six Month Mark | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/28/2026
items.content: <article>"Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Mattie Duppler, Senior Fellow for Fiscal Policy at the National Taxpayers Union, says Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments on interest rates were the “least interesting” part of his Jackson Hole speech and points instead to his focus on the availability of credit. Democratic Representative Lori Trahan of Massachusetts discusses her bipartisan FRONTIER Act, which aims to create federal oversight of the most advanced AI models through reporting, independent audits, and emergency safeguards. Sec. Leon Panetta, former US Secretary of Defense, says the US is “now trapped in another forever war” with Iran after six months of fighting with “no end in sight.” (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: US to Take Control of Major Portion of Venezuelan Oil Wealth
items.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Eric Martin
items.content: <article>The US is set to take majority control over a huge amount of Venezuela’s oil wealth in an unprecedented maneuver that officials said would create the world’s second-largest private oil company by reserves and secure American petroleum supplies for decades to come.</article>

items.title: For Trump, the Iran War Is Stuck Between Combat and Genuine Peace
items.author: Peter Baker
items.content: <article>The war has deteriorated over the past six months into Mr. Trump’s own version of a “forever war,” with no clear goals and no end in sight.</article>

items.title: Milo Yiannopoulos, a Right-Wing Provocateur, Is Arrested by ICE
items.author: Chris Cameron, Hamed Aleaziz and Ken Bensinger
items.content: <article>Mr. Yiannopoulos, a prominent early supporter of President Trump, was detained at the New Orleans airport. The Trump administration publicized his arrest and shared a mug shot.</article>

items.title: Chevron Is in Talks to Expand in Venezuela, a Potential Win for Trump
items.author: Rebecca F. Elliott, Simon Romero, Anatoly Kurmanaev and Lisa Friedman
items.content: <article>President Trump’s administration has been pushing U.S. companies like Chevron to invest more in Venezuela’s oil industry.</article>

items.title: ICE Deports Right-Wing Provocateur, Influencer Milo Yiannopoulos
items.author: Alicia A. Caldwell
items.content: <article>Federal immigration authorities said they deported right-wing provocateur and online influencer Milo Yiannopoulos after he was detained and accused of overstaying his visa.</article>

items.title: California Sues Trump Administration Over Offshore Wind Cancellation
items.author: Heather Knight
items.content: <article>The state is asking a court to reverse a Trump administration agreement and reinstate a planned offshore wind farm.</article>

items.title: It’s Trump’s Capital Now, but Voters Aren’t Living in It
items.author: Elizabeth Williamson
items.content: <article>His obsession with remaking Washington might hurt his party politically.</article>

items.title: Trump Administration Appeals Ruling Halting Mail-In Voting Rules
items.author: Zach Montague
items.content: <article>The Postal Service appealed an emergency decision from Thursday that blocked it from changing its procedures for mail-in voting ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Uphold Ban on Transgender Troops
items.author: Ann E. Marimow and Dave Philipps
items.content: <article>President Trump issued an executive order barring transgender service members from the military as part of a broader attack on transgender rights.</article>
